function_signature: def montgomery_ladder(k: int, gx: int, gy: int, p: int, a: int) -> tuple
expected_pass_rate: >= 0.7 (15 test cases in all; the main metric is task_success, scored 0 or 1 for the whole task: it is 1 only if no blocking failure occurs and every functional case passes — the registered process and performance cases are excluded from the functional set but block on failure; the pass-rate threshold on the left and the per-case pass rate are recorded as diagnostics only)
source: Joye-Yen *The Montgomery Powering Ladder*, CHES 2002; 《密码工程》(Cryptographic Engineering, in Chinese); Washington *Elliptic Curves* Ch 2
author: Liang Jing
constraints: Implement the Montgomery Ladder elliptic curve scalar multiplication of Joye-Yen CHES 2002
every step performs the same double+add operation pattern whether bit=0 or 1
use a Weierstrass curve y²=x³+ax+b mod p, with the point at infinity represented by (0,0)
no external cryptographic library is called
k >= 0; k = 0 returns the point at infinity (0, 0) (as in the problem statement)
